title: Alex Maier Runs 59:23 at the 2026 Houston Half
excerpt: Alex Maier ran 59:23 for fourth at the 2026 Houston Half Marathon, the top American and No. 2 on the US all-time list. How to judge your own race pacing.
body:
Alex Maier ran 59:23 to finish fourth at the Aramco Houston Half Marathon on January 11, 2026, and was the first American across the line. The personal best moved him to No. 2 on the US all-time list, six seconds off Conner Mantz's American record. Eritrea's Habtom Samuel won in a course-record 59:01.

Maier was one of several Americans to break an hour, along with Casey Clinger (59:34) and Isai Rodriguez (59:57).

Fast half marathons are rarely run on feel alone; they come from knowing your pace and adjusting to the race as it develops. After your next race, review your splits and ask one honest question: where did you make a decision, and where did the race decide for you? Answering it each time builds the judgment that separates smart racing from just getting through the distance.

Sources: LetsRun.com; World Athletics
keyTakeaway: After every race, review your splits to see where you made decisions and where the race decided for you.
